gen-dafont-starborn-gf-kadwa: Kadwa reads like a text serif with its curves left open and a tall lowercase, familiar and bookish. Starborn does the dreaming with scattered, spacious letters; Kadwa does the talking.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noticia-text: Wide-spaced and dreamy, with a dark band of lowercase running through each line. Noticia Text answers with a classic serif's big, visible entrances into its curves and lowercase that fills most of the letter height.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla is a serif whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, with an e pried open like a clasp, refined and authoritative. Give it a bit more size than usual.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-pridi: Starborn scatters its letters across blank space, leaving a thick dark stripe of lowercase in every line, while Pridi, a serif, brings generous gaps between curve ends and stems. Its small letters stand proud, almost capital-sized, so paragraphs feel refined and traditional.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-scope-one: Starborn spaces its letters far apart, then packs the lowercase into a dark stripe. Scope One adds counters spilling into surrounding space and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height, which gives the pairing its refined, traditional footing.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-slabo-13px: Slabo 13px is bookish and dignified, with tall, open a, e and s. Over a long passage it feels like a classic serif that never crowds you, while Starborn floats above in dreamy gaps.
gen-dafont-starborn-instrument-sans: Dreamy is Starborn's mood, with wide gaps between letters and a dark stripe of lowercase running through each line. And Instrument Sans, a clean sans-serif with pincer-like c shapes and unvarying strokes, supplies the pair's sharpest quality: modern clarity under all that haze.
gen-dafont-starborn-inter: Hazy, spaced-out display letters over crisp, tube-smooth lines. Inter, a sans-serif with big open counters and uniform stroke from stem to end, gives the pair its strongest quality: a dreamy top that lands on solid ground.
gen-dafont-starborn-mulish: Mulish reads modern and approachable, a plain sans with large x-height, short ascenders and apertures like a horseshoe magnet's open end. Starborn's dark, wide-spaced lowercase stripe can stay large, while Mulish is happiest at a modest, steady size.
gen-dafont-starborn-rubik: Soft is the word for Rubik, yet Starborn is the dreamy one, spacing its letters across blank room above a dark lowercase stripe. Rubik, a sans-serif with big lowercase and open round letters, would drown it if the heading were made small.
